Note 1 – Basis of Presentation. The condensed consolidated financial statements include the accounts of Acme Widgets, Inc. and its wholly owned subsidiaries (collectively, the “Company”). The Company prepared them in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles for interim financial information. In the opinion of management, they reflect all adjustments of a normal, recurring nature necessary for a fair statement of the results for the interim periods presented. Operating results for the three months ended June 29, 2024 are not necessarily indicative of the results expected for the full fiscal year. These statements should be read together with the audited consolidated financial statements included in the Company’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 30, 2023.
Note 2 – Revenue. The Company recognizes revenue when control of a widget passes to the customer, which for most sales happens at shipment. Net revenue was $7,210 million from industrial widgets and $5,135 million from consumer widgets for the three months ended June 29, 2024. Deferred revenue, which consists mainly of prepaid maintenance contracts, was $412 million at quarter end, and the Company expects to recognize about 70% of it within twelve months.
Note 3 – Inventories. Inventories are stated at the lower of cost and net realizable value, with cost determined on a first-in, first-out basis. Finished goods were $1,102 million and raw materials were $388 million as of June 29, 2024.

Item 2. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
The following discussion should be read together with the condensed consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes in Part I, Item 1 of this Form 10-Q.
Overview. Acme Widgets designs, manufactures and sells widgets for industrial and consumer customers in more than forty countries. The Company’s fiscal year is the 52- or 53-week period that ends on the last Saturday of December.
Results of Operations. Net revenue increased 12% to $12,345 million in the quarter, driven by higher industrial widget volumes and price increases that took effect in March. Gross margin percentage rose to 45.0% from 44.5% a year earlier because lower freight costs more than offset higher wages at the Dayton plant. Operating expenses grew 6% as the Company added engineers to its sensor program.
Item 1A of the Company’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for fiscal 2023 describes the risks that could affect these results; there have been no material changes to those risks other than the ones described in Part II, Item 1A below.
Liquidity and Capital Resources. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $3,870 million at quarter end. The Company believes its balances, together with cash generated by operations and its $1,500 million revolving credit facility, will be sufficient to fund working capital, capital expenditures of about $900 million this fiscal year, and the quarterly dividend for at least the next twelve months. During the quarter the Company repurchased 2.1 million shares for $240 million under the program announced in February.

PART II — OTHER INFORMATION
Item 1. Legal Proceedings
The Company is subject to legal proceedings and claims that arise in the ordinary course of business. Management does not expect the outcome of any pending matter to have a material adverse effect on the Company’s financial position.

Item 1A. Risk Factors

The Company’s business, reputation, results of operations and financial condition can be affected by a number of factors, whether currently known or unknown, including those described below. The risks below update the risk factors disclosed in the Annual Report.

Supply of specialty steel. The Company buys most of its specialty steel from two suppliers in Ohio. A disruption at either supplier, a strike, or a sharp increase in steel prices could delay shipments and reduce gross margin, and the Company may not be able to find alternative sources quickly or at similar cost.

Customer concentration. Sales to the Company’s three largest distributors made up 38% of net revenue in the quarter. The loss of any of them, or a significant reduction in their orders, could materially reduce net revenue.

Currency exposure. About one third of net revenue is earned in euros and yen. A stronger U.S. dollar reduces the dollar value of those sales, and the Company’s hedging program covers only part of the exposure for the next twelve months.

Cybersecurity incidents. The Company relies on information systems to run its plants and to process orders. An attack that disables these systems could halt production, expose customer data and lead to regulatory penalties, litigation and remediation costs that insurance may not fully cover.

Item 7.Supplementary Information
Segment information. The Company reports two segments: Industrial Widgets and Consumer Widgets. Segment operating income excludes stock-based compensation, restructuring charges and corporate costs, which management does not allocate to the segments when it assesses performance.
Industrial Widgets operating income was $2,410 million in the quarter, up from $2,080 million a year earlier, on higher volumes of the model X-200 sold to automotive customers. Consumer Widgets operating income was $905 million compared with $930 million, as promotional pricing in Europe lowered average selling prices.
Backlog. Orders for industrial widgets that the Company expects to ship within twelve months were $4,300 million at quarter end, compared with $3,950 million at the end of the prior quarter. Backlog is not necessarily indicative of future net revenue because customers may cancel orders before shipment.
Employees. The Company had approximately 18,400 full-time employees at quarter end, of whom about 7,600 work outside the United States. Voluntary turnover was 6% on an annualized basis, compared with 8% a year earlier.
Properties. The Company owns manufacturing plants in Dayton, Ohio; Monterrey, Mexico; and Brno, Czech Republic, and leases distribution centers in eleven countries. Management believes these facilities are suitable and adequate for current operations and for the growth it expects over the next two years.
